## Tone guide

Reader should feel after finishing an article:

- **Trustworthy**: claims come with evidence
- **Practical**: examples over abstractions
- **Honest**: limitations stated, no overpromising

## Voice rules

- **How to say it**: explain technical topics in plain language; assume a curious but non-expert reader
- **What not to do**: avoid hype words ("revolutionary", "ultimate"), avoid first-person ("we believe"), avoid unsourced stats
- **Sentence style**: short and direct; one idea per sentence
- **Citation style**: Markdown links `[label](url)`; cite .gov/.edu for regulatory claims; cite real standards (ISO/IEC/FDA) where applicable

## Forbidden phrases (synthetic example)

> ❌ "In today's fast-paced world..."
> ❌ "Studies show..." (without a source)
> ❌ "Everyone knows..."
> ❌ "We are committed to..."
> ✅ "FDA 21 CFR 1040.10 limits..."
> ✅ "OSHA 1926.54 requires..."
> ✅ "Per [NIST publication X](https://...), the value is..."
